I quickly checked Prysm's [`GetProposerDuties`](https://github.com/OffchainLabs/prysm/blob/af7afba26e2a4fc41f28a555b69882d4f1d77c28/beacon-chain/rpc/eth/validator/handlers.go#L982) func & it doesn't look like they do. looking into it now are most of the bootstrap nodes in https://github.com/ethpandaops/fusaka-devnets/blob/master/network-configs/devnet-3/metadata/bootstrap_nodes.txt supposed to be (as far as I can tell) unresponsive? We have a tool `dcli` to just query some basic discv5 things and: e.g., ``` TRC 2025-07-25 14:43:24.778+00:00 Send message packet topics="eth p2p discv5" tid=33940 file=protocol.nim:624 dstId=65*570f81 address=209.38.198.0:9000 kind=findNode No Nodes message returned ``` we do. Now that i'm looking into it, does `dependent_root` still make sense under fulu? awesome thanks for clarifying! fwiw, if we want eth_config to be in the eth namespace i think we should withdraw eth_config EIP and open it as a PR to the execution-apis i'm also curious if anyone has considered the downstream implications if clients begin serving all the config info. historically, it has not been possible to know as someone interacting with the API what particular fork and particular chain is on unless the client also has some knowledge of the forks i also don't understand why the precompiles are a map of addr -> name whereas the system contracts are name -> addr just a weird inconsistency imo I will create a parallel PR for execution-apis We are serving the configurations, not the fork name. The way to sus out what fork can also be done via eth_call for the most part and other calls to probe the locations. The format is <what is being configured> = <the configuration>. For precompiles since we start from 0 and increment one-by-one what we are configuring is if the next precompile set is activated. For system contracts we are configuring where certain contracts are. There was a proposal to make it address->name, but for system contracts that had bad usability because we then had to search for system contract names. I'm open to flipping it for precompiles to be name->address, but when I made that offer in the PR proposing the change it was passed over and the current format is used. I'll get a Geth PR for eth_config out today, based on the current spec. - https://github.com/shemnon/go-ethereum/tree/eip-7910-eth_config are most of the bootstrap nodes in https hey folks, JFYI. we have mev-boost blocks coming in for Fulu: http://mev-relay-1.fusaka-devnet-3.ethpandaops.io:9060/ they are fairly frequent with some getHeader calls returning with `no bid found` which is not very harmful also note that, this MEV boost relay has the V2 getPayload API implemented https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/pull/123 yeah its super useful for testing sync, can we run it until monday atleast? also why don't we just serialize to rlp and hash that? bringing json canocialization into the mix seems unneccessary i think it's already dead :))) RLP is not human readable, and IIRC we wanto to sunset RLP, so if it wasn't directly human readable it would need to be SSZ. For a debugging aide, we can skip the fork ID and just diff the JSON without anyhing more than a formatter. The tooling to make sense of RLP and SSZ is much more opaque. sure but we can still represent the RLP in json like we do for other protocol types, no? An an argument for "why not SSZ" is also an argument for the whole of the JSON-RPC to be SSZ. I'm on-board if it's across-the-board RLP is a format marked for death, let's not use it anymore. excerpts.content:
RLP is not human readable, and IIRC we wanto to sunset RLP, so if it wasn't directly human readable it would need to be SSZ.

For a debugging aide, we can skip the fork ID and just diff the JSON without anyhing more than a formatter. The tooling to make sense of RLP and SSZ is much more opaque.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: sure but we can still represent the RLP in json like we do for other protocol types, no?

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: An an argument for "why not SSZ" is also an argument for the whole of the JSON-RPC to be SSZ. I'm on-board if it's across-the-board

excerpts.author: _shemnon
excerpts.content: RLP is a format marked for death, let's not use it anymore.
